findings.summary: docs/system-facts.md is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: Half of the new anchor test will fail. It requires the reference doc to contain none of the anchor phrases, but the anchors are short topic phrases that the doc's planned content has to use.
findings.evidence: Decision 9 builds the anchors from decision 4: lib.rs:441-543 includes 'governance file' (lib.rs:453) and '.github/workflows/' (lib.rs:446); briefs.rs:1587/1616 include 'seam, fake or fixture' and 'refusal_corpus'; the severity anchors are 'blocker (', 'major (', 'minor (', 'nit ('. The planned doc holds a 'governance file list', 'plan-field examples' (demonstrations and the refusal corpus, see planner.md:13-14) and 'worked examples per severity', and step 3 says each section names where its rule is enforced. A list of governance files can hardly avoid '.github/workflows/', and explaining demonstrations can hardly avoid 'seam, fake or fixture'. So either the test fails, or the doc is written around arbitrary substrings. That is a rule that misfires on ordinary words. The absence check also adds no protection: the presence-in-frame assertion already guarantees no listed rule exists only in the doc. Fix: Keep the presence assertions: each anchor in its composed frame, the conditional pointer once per common frame, none in the capability sections, and the file exists. Drop the 'doc contains none of the anchors' assertion. If a guard against copying rules into the doc is still wanted, check only whole rule lines (full list-item lines of the frames, such as the severity lines) and not short phrases. Update decision 9, step 8, the criterion 4 demonstration and the doc description to match.
findings.location: Decision 9; Steps 3 and 8; Files: docs/agent-reference.md; Demonstration for criterion 4

findings.summary: An incidental test assertion sets a floor on how short the verifier prompt can get, and the fallback 'keep the verifier frame longer' works against the request.
findings.evidence: run_pin_tests.rs:1614-1618 asserts left == 0 only so that the rendered '{used} of {budget} tokens used, {left} left' row is checked (line 1620). It does not encode a design rule about prompt length. The plan builds the inequality 0.1·C + K < 0.8·V around it and forbids trimming VERIFIER_FRAME. Re-derived: C≈277, V≈433, K≈267 gives a set of about 977, a budget of 1100, and contract plus two frames of about 1143, so the main targets do work. Fix: Keep the current targets. For the fallback, treat that one assertion as a forced edit, as with docs/system-facts.md: make the test compose a third VERIFIER_FRAME, or assert the computed 'left' value in the rendered row, and note it in the CHANGELOG. Do not lengthen a prompt to keep a test fixture over budget.

findings.summary: The criterion 4 demonstration also runs `ls docs/agent-reference.md`, which may not be among the commands the verifier's brief allows, and repeats what the test already checks.
findings.evidence: The new test already asserts that CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/../../docs/agent-reference.md is a file. The verifier frame (verifier.md:14) limits Bash to the brief's commands. Fix: Drop the `ls` step and rely on the test's existence assertion.

summary: The plan matches the request and the accepted reading. What I checked against the code: the budget arithmetic is correct (Verifier 1100, about 89%, with about 43 tokens of margin over the contract-plus-two-frames check at run_pin_tests.rs:1618; Producer 1050, about 88%); the dependents list covers every reader I found (budgets.rs, run_pin_tests.rs, the lib.rs wording tests, briefs.rs anchors, verify.rs, mirrors, cap-study headings, CHANGELOG readers); the docs/system-facts.md edit is forced by system_facts_budgets_match_computed; the padded set in an_over_budget_role_set_fails (about 1600 tokens) stays over the new budgets. One major soundness problem remains. The new test asserts that the reference doc contains none of the anchor phrases, but those anchors are short topic phrases such as 'governance file', '.github/workflows/', 'seam, fake or fixture', 'refusal_corpus' and 'major ('. The doc's planned sections (governance file list, plan-field examples, severity examples, where each rule is enforced) have to use these words, so the test fails or the doc is written around substrings. That check also adds nothing beyond the presence-in-frame check. Two smaller issues: the fallback lets a test assertion set a floor on the verifier prompt's length, and the criterion 4 demonstration includes an `ls` the verifier may not be allowed to run. Verdict: revise.
